label: alg:witness-json-pipeline
title: Witness-JSON pipeline (cross-language interchange)
html:
Algorithm. Witness-JSON pipeline (cross-language interchange)

Algorithm (Witness-JSON pipeline). Cross-language interchange contract for *.witness.json files emitted by canonical compute scripts via the WitnessBuilder API. Maintained as a sidecar to the canonical chain because every chain step's computation.witness field points to a file that conforms to this contract, apart from a residue of older witnesses that do not yet conform.

Required JSON shape (WitnessBuilder.build() output)

{
  "engine":           "python",
  "engineVersion":    "...",
  "computedAt":       "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+00:00",
  "commitSha":        "<git head sha>",
  "scriptFile":       "<script>.py",
  "scriptHash":       "<content sha256>",
  "scriptCommitSha":  "<git file sha>",
  "durationMs":       0,
  "assertions":       [{ "name": "...", "passed": true, "delta": "..." }],
  "allPassed":        true,
  "computation":      "<witness name>",
  "precisionMetadata": {
    "compute_dps":      65,
    "output_dps":       50,
    "guard_digits":     15,
    "truncation_bound": "1e-50"
  },
  "environment":      { ... },
  "parameters":       { ... },
  "data":             { ... },
  "caveats":          [ ... ]
}

Precision discipline

  • Default compute: 70 dps mpmath (qou_substrate.precision.COMPUTE_DPS).
  • Default serialisation: 60 dps (qou_substrate.precision.OUTPUT_DPS), with a guard of 10 (PRECISION_GUARD, the difference between the two).
  • Cross-method assertion at \leq 10^{-15} relative agreement (L1 — internal compute precision).
  • The precisionMetadata block records the truncation bound so downstream consumers know the error floor of every serialised value.

LP/SDP duals

If the compute is LP / SDP / operator-selection, the witness must additionally carry the fields specified in alg:lp-sdp-dual-emission.

Wedderburn-respecting witnesses

Every per-partition computation (Step 5 and downstream Step 9b) must record the partition tag \lambda alongside each value via builder.add_data(...), so the witness is partition-respecting and reviewers can check the isotypic structure.

Algorithm

1. Initialize WitnessBuilder(name, engine="python+mpmath").
2. builder.add_parameter(key, value) for each input parameter.
3. builder.add_data(key, value) for each computed output
   (per-partition tags included where relevant).
4. builder.add_assertion(name, condition_callable, description)
   for each correctness check.
5. builder.add_caveat(text) for any known limitation.
6. builder.add_upstream(path) for each upstream witness whose
   hash must be tracked for drift.
7. builder.save() emits the JSON to the canonical location.

Correctness conditions

  1. The Wedderburn decomposition (prop:wedderburn-trace-identity) defines the partition structure that add_data records.
  2. The LP/SDP dual contract (prop:operator-selection-lp) defines the dual-emission fields used by Step 10.

Canonical entry point

from qou_substrate.witness import WitnessBuilder

w = WitnessBuilder(name="my-result", engine="python+mpmath")
w.add_parameter("q0", q0_value)
w.add_data("tau_M", tau_M_value)
w.add_assertion(
    "1ppQ_cross_method",
    condition=lambda: abs(a - b) < mp.mpf("1e-15"),
    description="cross-method agreement at L1",
)
w.save()

Witness contract (meta)

Every *.witness.json is checked on three counts: the LP/SDP dual fields (lp_dual_witness_validator.py), an explicit q-regime declaration, and staleness against the current q_0. A stale or schema-violating witness is rejected, not consumed.

Notes

Cross-language sibling: the witness-schema PyPI + npm package provides Zod / Pydantic / TypeScript types for every canonical witness shape, so Pyodide / Node / TS callers see the same contract.
